questions.title: String Compression
questions.statement: Given an array of characters **chars**, compress it in-place. For every consecutive group of equal characters, write the character once; if the group length is greater than 1, write the decimal digits of its length after the character. Return the new length.\n\nThe first returned-length characters of chars must contain the compressed string. Group lengths of 10 or more are written as separate digits. Use only constant extra space.
questions.inputFormat: A single line containing the character sequence without commas or quotes. For example, aabbccc represents ["a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "c", "c"].
questions.constraints: 1 <= chars.length <= 2000\nEach character is a lowercase letter, uppercase letter, digit, or symbol.

questions.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
questions.statement: Given a string **s** of length n consisting of uppercase English letters and an integer **k**, you may perform at most k operations. In one operation, change any character in the string to any other uppercase English letter.\n\nReturn the length of the longest substring that can be transformed into a string containing only identical characters using at most k operations.
questions.inputFormat: The first line contains the uppercase string s.\nThe second line contains the integer k.
questions.outputFormat: Print the maximum possible length of a uniform-character substring.
questions.constraints: 1 <= n, k <= 10^5\ns contains uppercase English letters only.

questions.title: Smallest Window in a String Containing all the Characters of Another String
questions.statement: Given two strings **s** and **t**, return the minimum window substring of s that contains every character in t, including duplicate characters. If no such substring exists, return the empty string.\n\nThe test cases guarantee that the answer, when it exists, is unique.
questions.inputFormat: The first line contains s.\nThe second line contains t.
questions.outputFormat: Print the minimum window substring, or an empty line if no valid window exists.
questions.constraints: 1 <= s.length, t.length <= 10^5\ns and t contain uppercase and lowercase English letters.

questions.title: Wildcard String Matching
questions.statement:
Given an input string **s** and a pattern **p**, implement wildcard pattern matching with support for \`?\` and \`*\`.

- \`?\` matches any single character.
- \`*\` matches any sequence of characters, including the empty sequence.

The match must cover the **entire** input string, not only a substring. Return \`true\` if \`p\` matches \`s\`; otherwise return \`false\`.
questions.inputFormat: The first line contains the string s.\nThe second line contains the pattern p.
questions.outputFormat: Print true if the entire string matches the pattern; otherwise print false.
questions.constraints: 0 <= s.length, p.length <= 2000\ns contains lowercase English letters only.\np contains lowercase English letters, ? or *.

questions.title: Longest Prefix Suffix
questions.statement: Given a lowercase English string **s**, find the length of the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix of s.\n\nA prefix and suffix may overlap, but they must not be equal to the entire string.
questions.inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
questions.outputFormat: Print the length of the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix.
questions.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 10^6\ns contains lowercase English letters only.

questions.title: Rabin-Karp Algorithm for Pattern Searching
questions.statement:
Given two strings: a text string in which you want to search, and a pattern string that you are looking for within the text. Return all positions (0-based indexing) where the pattern occurs as a substring in the text. If the pattern does not occur, return an empty list.

![Rabin-Karp pattern matching example](/rabin-karp-pattern-search.png)

Use the Rabin-Karp rolling-hash technique. Verify matching hash windows character by character to avoid collisions.
questions.inputFormat: The first line contains the text string.\nThe second line contains the pattern string.
questions.outputFormat: Print the 0-based starting indices in the format [i, j, ...]. Print [] when there are no matches.
questions.constraints: 1 <= text.length <= 10^5\n1 <= pattern.length <= text.length\nBoth strings contain lowercase English letters.
